name: Samter Triad (Aspirin-Exacerbated Respiratory Disease)

criteria.description: Presence of asthma diagnosed by clinical history and pulmonary function tests
Presence of nasal polyps confirmed by nasal endoscopy or imaging
Respiratory reaction to aspirin or other COX-1 inhibitors confirmed by history or aspirin challenge
Chronic inflammation of the nasal and sinus mucosa with symptoms lasting >12 weeks

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: asthma, nasal polyposis, and aspirin sensitivity
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Aspirin challenge testing is the gold standard for confirming aspirin sensitivity when history is unclear.

pathognomonic.notes: Triggered by aspirin or other COX-1 inhibitors
Bilateral nasal polyps causing nasal obstruction
Often severe and difficult to control

common.notes: Mucus drainage from nasal cavity to throat

occasional.notes: Reduced or lost sense of smell
Shortness of breath during physical activity

rare.notes: Nausea or abdominal pain after aspirin ingestion
Severe systemic allergic reaction to aspirin

laboratory: Elevated eosinophil count in peripheral blood
Increased urinary leukotriene E4 during aspirin challenge
imaging: CT scan showing bilateral nasal polyposis and sinus opacification
Chest X-ray or CT may show airway inflammation
genetic: No specific genetic marker identified; possible HLA associations under investigation
other: Positive aspirin challenge test confirming aspirin sensitivity
Pulmonary function tests showing reversible airway obstruction

distinguishingFeatures: Less severe asthma or absent asthma
Systemic vasculitis signs (e.g., purpura, renal involvement)

redFlags: Severe aspirin-induced bronchospasm causing respiratory distress
Rapid progression of nasal polyposis with airway obstruction
references: Stevenson DD, et al. Aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease: prevalence, diagnosis, and management. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2014.
Laidlaw TM, et al. Aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease: pathophysiology and treatment. Allergy Asthma Proc. 2018.
Bachert C, et al. European Position Paper on Rhinosinusitis and Nasal Polyps 2020.
